docs.title: Welcome to Desktop-D30
docs.text: Desktop-D30 is a professional label design and printing application specifically designed for the Phomemo D30 Bluetooth label printer.

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
• Intuitive Design Canvas: Drag and drop text, shapes, QR codes, and barcodes.
  • Sharp Printing: High-resolution rendering ensures scannable codes.
  • Batch Printing: Load CSV data to print hundreds of labels in seconds.
  • Cross-Platform: Supports Linux and Windows.

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text: To begin, select your label size from the top menu and start adding objects from the side inspector!

docs.title: Architecture Guide
docs.text: This document provides a high-level technical overview of how Desktop-D30 is structured. It is intended for developers who want to understand the "soul" of the application beyond individual function definitions.

docs.title: 1. Core Data Model (types.h)
docs.text:
The application follows a simple, flat data model.

  • LabelObject: The atom of the application. It contains position, size, rotation, and type-specific data (text, image paths, etc.).
    • Key Feature: It stores its own texture handle for images/barcodes to ensure they aren't re-generated every frame.
  • Project: A container for a collection of LabelObjects, the selected label size, and CSV data.
  • InteractionState: Manages the "Editor" state, including the selection list, clipboard, and the Undo/Redo stacks.

docs.title: 2. The Rendering Pipeline (rendering.cpp)
docs.text: There are two distinct rendering paths in Desktop-D30:

docs.title: A. Real-time Canvas (UI)
docs.text:
1. The editor uses Raylib's Camera2D to provide zooming and panning.
  2. Each object is rendered via RENDERING::RenderObject.
  3. Rotation Logic: Objects are rotated around their top-left (x, y) coordinate using standard 2D rotation matrices. UI interaction (clicking/dragging) uses an inverse rotation matrix to map mouse coordinates back into the object's local space for accurate collision detection.

docs.title: B. Print Generation (Thermal)
docs.text:
1. Buffer Allocation: The project is rendered to an off-screen Image buffer matching the physical dimensions of the label (e.g., 240x96 pixels).
  2. Thresholding: The color image is converted to grayscale and then to 1-bit black/white using a weighted threshold (0.299R, 0.587G, 0.114B).
  3. Rasterization: The 1-bit pixels are packed into rows where each byte represents 8 horizontal pixels, conforming to the Phomemo D30's RFCOMM protocol.

docs.title: 3. Input & History (input.cpp)
docs.text:
The interaction system is designed for both mouse precision and keyboard speed.

  • Undo/Redo: The system uses a "State Snapshot" approach. Before any destructive or significant change, the entire Project object is serialized and pushed onto the undoStack (limited to 50 steps). This is inefficient for memory but extremely robust for complex layout changes.
  • Snapping: The HandleObjectDrag function implements a dual-mode snapping system:
    • Grid Snap: Rounds coordinates to the nearest 20-unit increment.
    • Object Snap: Scans all other objects and "snaps" if edges or centers are within a 5-unit threshold.

docs.title: 4. Cross-Platform Bluetooth (protocol.cpp / printer.cpp)
docs.text:
The Bluetooth layer is abstracted to handle the vast differences between Linux and Windows drivers.

  • Linux (BlueZ): Uses standard POSIX socket calls (socket, connect, write) with AF_BLUETOOTH and BTPROTO_RFCOMM.
  • Windows (Winsock2): Uses the BTHPROTO_RFCOMM protocol. It requires initializing the Winsock library (WSAStartup) and uses send instead of write.
  • Protocol Layer: The Protocol namespace handles the higher-level "D30 Language"—specifically the header packets, row-by-row image data, and the "End of Print" commands.

docs.title: 5. Asset Management (assets.cpp)
docs.text:
To keep the UI snappy, assets are managed through a single AssetManager singleton.

  • Lazy Loading: Fonts and icon thumbnails are only loaded into VRAM when they are first needed or when the library is opened.
  • Background Load Queue: During the splash screen, the app initializes a queue of all icon paths. It processes 10 icons per frame during the main loop to prevent the UI from freezing while loading hundreds of tiny textures.

docs.title: 6. Project Serialization
docs.text: Projects are saved as .d30 files, which are standard JSON. The application uses the nlohmann::json library to automate the conversion between C++ structs and JSON text. This allows users to easily inspect or even manually edit project files if needed.

docs.title: Managing Assets
docs.text: Desktop-D30 allows you to customize your labels with your own fonts, icons, and decorative borders.

docs.title: Custom Fonts
docs.text:
You can use any .ttf or .otf font file in your designs.

  1. Select a Text or Data Field object on your canvas.
  2. In the Side Inspector, under the Properties section, click Import Font....
  3. Select your font file.
  4. Your font is now permanently available in the Font dropdown menu under the "User Fonts" section.

System Fonts

Desktop-D30 also automatically detects fonts already installed on your Windows or Linux system.

docs.title: Icon Library
docs.text: The Icon Library is where you store and organize small graphics used in your labels.

docs.title: Importing Icons
docs.text:
1. Go to Assets -> Manage Icon Library.
  2. Click Import Icons... and select one or more image files (.png, .jpg, .bmp).
  3. These icons will now appear in the Add Icon popup on the sidebar.

docs.title: Organizing Icons
docs.text: In the Icon Manager, you can: * Tag Icons: Add descriptive tags to icons to make them searchable. * Rename: Give icons custom display names. * Categories: Move icons into different folders/categories using the "Move to Category" dropdown.

docs.title: Deco Borders
docs.text: Decorative borders are special graphics that frame your label.

docs.title: Importing Borders
docs.text:
1. Go to Assets -> Manage Deco Borders.
  2. Click Import Borders... and select your border images.
  3. These will now be available when using the Deco Border tool in the sidebar.

Scaling Borders

When you add a Deco Border, the application automatically scales it to fit your current label size. You can adjust its thickness and corner radius in the Properties panel.

docs.title: Batch Printing with CSV
docs.text: Batch printing allows you to create many labels at once using data from a spreadsheet.

docs.title: Preparing your CSV
docs.text:
1. Create a spreadsheet with headers (e.g., Product, Price, SKU).
  2. Fill in your data rows.
  3. Save the file as a .csv (Comma Separated Values).

docs.title: Setting up Data Fields
docs.text:
1. In Desktop-D30, go to File -> Load CSV Data... and select your file.
  2. Click Add Object -> Data Field.
  3. In the Inspector, select the column name from your CSV that you want to link to this field.
  4. You can navigate through your data using the navigator at the bottom of the screen to preview how each label will look.

docs.title: Printing
docs.text: Once you are happy with the layout, go to File -> Batch Print. Select the range of rows you wish to print and click Start Print.

docs.title: Development & Build Guide
docs.text: This guide is for developers who want to compile Desktop-D30 from source or contribute to the project.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text: Regardless of your operating system, you will need: * CMake (3.14 or higher) * C++17 Compiler (GCC 9+, Clang 10+, or MSVC 2019+) * Git (to clone the repository and dependencies)

docs.title: Linux Dependencies
docs.text:
On Debian-based systems (Ubuntu, Mint, etc.), install the following:

sudo apt update
sudo apt install build-essential cmake git libbluetooth-dev libasound2-dev libx11-dev libxrandr-dev libxi-dev libxcursor-dev libxinerama-dev libxkbcommon-dev

docs.title: Compiling on Linux (Native)
docs.text: We provide a Makefile wrapper for common CMake commands.

docs.title: Debug Build
docs.text:
make build

This will generate the executable in build/Desktop-D30.

docs.title: Running the App
docs.text: make run

docs.title: Running Tests
docs.text: make run_tests

docs.title: Cross-Compiling for Windows from Linux
docs.text:
You can generate a Windows .exe directly from a Linux machine using the MinGW-w64 toolchain.

  1. Install the toolchain: bash sudo apt install mingw-w64
  2. Run the cross-compile command: bash make cross-windows This will create a build_win_cross/ directory containing Desktop-D30.exe.

docs.title: Using MinGW-w64
docs.text:
1. Install w64devkit or a similar MinGW distribution.
  2. Open your terminal and navigate to the project folder.
  3. Run: bash mkdir build cd build cmake -G "MinGW Makefiles" .. make

docs.title: Generating Linux Installers
docs.text:
To create .deb and .tar.gz packages for Linux:

./build_release.sh

The installers will be placed in the build/ directory. This script uses CPack internally.

docs.title: Project Structure
docs.text:
• src/: C++ source files.
  • include/: Header files.
  • assets/: Built-in icons, borders, and fonts.
  • docs/: Documentation source (Markdown).
  • tests/: Unit tests using GoogleTest.
  • cmake/: Custom CMake toolchains and scripts.

docs.title: Installation Guide
docs.text: Desktop-D30 is available for both Linux and Windows.

docs.title: Windows
docs.text:
1. Download the latest Desktop-D30.exe from the releases page.
  2. Ensure the assets/ folder is located in the same directory as the .exe file.
  3. Simply double-click the .exe to run. No installation is required.

docs.title: Debian/Ubuntu (.deb)
docs.text:
1. Download the .deb package.
  2. Install using your package manager: bash sudo apt install ./Desktop-D30-1.0.0-Linux.deb

docs.title: Generic Linux (.tar.gz)
docs.text:
1. Extract the archive to a folder of your choice.
  2. Run the Desktop-D30 executable directly.

docs.title: Building from Source
docs.text: If you wish to compile the application yourself, please refer to the Development & Build Guide.

docs.title: Understanding the Interface
docs.text: The Desktop-D30 interface is designed to keep your focus on the label design.

docs.title: Main Canvas
docs.text: The center of the screen is your label canvas. * Navigation: Use the mouse wheel to zoom and Right-Click + Drag to pan the view. * Selection: Click an object to select it. Hold Shift to select multiple objects. * Modification: Drag the handles on the corners of a selected object to resize it.

docs.title: Side Inspector
docs.text: The panel on the left is your primary control center. It is divided into several sections:

docs.title: Project Settings
docs.text:
• Canvas Size: Choose the physical dimensions of your label (e.g., 12mm x 40mm).
  • Show Grid: Toggle the visual alignment grid.
  • Dark Mode: Switch between light and dark user interface themes.

docs.title: Data Source
docs.text: This section only appears after you have loaded a CSV file via File -> Load CSV Data. * Use the << and >> buttons to flip through your data rows. * The canvas will update in real-time to show how your label looks with actual data.

docs.title: Object Tree
docs.text: A list of all objects currently on your canvas. * Selection: Click an item in the tree to select it on the canvas. * Z-Order: Objects at the bottom of the list are drawn on top of objects at the top of the list.

docs.title: Properties Panel
docs.text: This section updates dynamically based on what you have selected. * Common: Adjust the precise X and Y coordinates. * Text/Field: Change font size, font family, and the text content. * Shapes: Adjust line thickness and dimensions. * Images/Icons: Change width, height, or swap the image file. * Barcode/QR: Adjust the size and the encoded data.

docs.title: Tools
docs.text: A grid of buttons to quickly add new elements: * Basics: Text and Data Fields. * Media: QR Codes and Barcodes. * Graphics: Custom Images and searchable Icons. * Shapes: Lines, Rectangles, and Circles. * Decor: Full-label Deco Borders.

docs.title: Menu Bar
docs.text:
• File: Save and Load your projects, or load CSV data.
  • Edit: Access Undo, Redo, Cut, Copy, and Paste commands.
  • Assets: Manage your local icon and border libraries.
  • Printer: Connect to your D30 device via Bluetooth.
  • Help: Access this user guide and application information.

docs.title: Bluetooth Printing
docs.text: Desktop-D30 connects directly to your Phomemo D30 printer using Bluetooth Classic.

docs.title: On Windows
docs.text:
1. Ensure your D30 printer is turned on.
  2. Open the Printer menu in Desktop-D30.
  3. Select Scan for Devices.
  4. Find your printer in the list (usually appears as D30_XXXX) and click Connect.
  5. Once the status indicator turns green, you are ready to print.

Driver Note

On Windows, you do not need to install any special drivers. Desktop-D30 uses the standard Windows Bluetooth stack.

docs.title: On Linux
docs.text:
1. Ensure your D30 printer is turned on.
  2. Go to the Printer menu and select Scan for Devices.
  3. Choose your printer and click Connect.

Bluetooth Permissions

If the application cannot find your Bluetooth adapter on Linux, ensure your user is in the lp or bluetooth group: sudo usermod -aG bluetooth $USER (reboot required after running).

docs.title: Printing Labels
docs.text:
Once connected, you can print the current canvas by going to Printer -> Print Single Label.

For printing multiple labels from a data source, see the Batch Printing guide.

docs.title: Keyboard & Mouse Shortcuts
docs.text: Efficiency is key when designing labels. Desktop-D30 supports a wide array of shortcuts for power users who prefer the keyboard.

docs.title: General Shortcuts
docs.text: Shortcut Action Ctrl + S Save current project Ctrl + L Load project Alt + F4 Exit application

docs.title: Adding Objects
docs.text: Shortcut Action Alt + T Add Text Object Alt + F Add Data Field Alt + Q Add QR Code Alt + B Add Barcode Alt + L Add Line Alt + R Add Rectangle Alt + C Add Circle Alt + D Add Border

docs.title: Editing & Rotation
docs.text: Shortcut Action Ctrl + Z Undo last action (up to 50 steps) Ctrl + Y Redo last undone action Ctrl + Shift + Z Alternative Redo shortcut Ctrl + C Copy selected objects Ctrl + X Cut selected objects Ctrl + V Paste objects from clipboard Delete / Backspace Remove selected objects Ctrl + [ Rotate selection Counter-Clockwise (15°) Ctrl + ] Rotate selection Clockwise (15°) Ctrl + Shift + [ Rotate selection CCW (90°) Ctrl + Shift + ] Rotate selection CW (90°)

docs.title: Precision Nudging
docs.text:
When one or more objects are selected, you can use the arrow keys for fine-grained movement:

  • Arrow Keys: Move selection by 1 unit.
  • Shift + Arrow Keys: Move selection by 10 units.

docs.title: Printing
docs.text: Shortcut Action Ctrl + P Print Single Label Ctrl + Shift + B Open Batch Print dialog Ctrl + Shift + P Open Sequence Print dialog

docs.title: Canvas & View
docs.text: Shortcut Action Ctrl + G Toggle Background Grid Ctrl + H Toggle Snapping (Grid & Objects) Mouse Wheel Zoom in and out Space + Left Drag Pan the canvas Right Click & Drag Pan the canvas Shift + Left Click Multi-select toggle
